newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to use oil bonanza to pay-off wage hike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to use oil bonanza to pay-off wage hike.

text.p: The Venezuelan Finance Minister said the government would use a 700 billion bolivar ($1.5 billion) windfall from high oil prices last year to pay- off a 70 percent public sector wage increase agreed in February.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azcoar said total unbudgeted payments for the year reached 930 billion bolivars, most of which derived from wage agreements. In addition to the oil revenues, 70 billion bolivars of the payments would be met from past gasoline price increases and another 259 billion bolivars from budget cuts and sales tax increases, he said.

"These are just some of the resources in the treasury that we can already count on," Matos said in Finance Ministry press release. The government had previously said it would use the oil windfall to pay down debt.
Matos added that 120 billion bolivars had been earmarked to meet severance payments to public sector workers due this year under a social security reform bill currently under discussion in Congress.
A further 110 billion bolivars would be allocated to education, and some 270 billion for regional governments.
